{{Nihongo|'''Watatsu Shrine'''|度津神社|Watatsu-jinja}}  is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the Hamochiiioka neighborhood of the city of {{ill|Sado, Niigata|ar|سادو (نييغاتا)|azb|سادو، نیقاتا|ce|Садо (Ниигата)|ceb|Sado Shi|cs|Sado (město)|de|Sado (Niigata)|el|Σάντο (Ιαπωνία)|eo|Sado (Niigata)|es|Sado (Niigata)|eu|Sado uhartea|fa|سادو، نیگاتا|fi|Sado (Niigata)|fr|Sado (préfecture de Niigata)|gl|Sado, Niigata|ha|Sado, Niigata|id|Sado, Niigata|it|Sado (città)|ja|佐渡市|ko|사도시|la|Sado (urbs)|lt|Sadas (Niigata)|ml|സാഡോ ദ്വീപ്|ms|Sado, Niigata|mzn|سادو، نیگاتا|nl|Sado (stad)|no|Sado (Niigata)|pl|Sado (Japonia)|pt|Sado (Niigata)|ro|Sado|ru|Садо (Ниигата)|simple|Sado, Niigata|sr|Садо|sv|Sado (stad)|tg|Садо, Ниигата|th|ซาโดะ|tl|Sado, Niigata|tr|Sado, Niigata|tt|Садо (Ниигата)|uk|Садо (Ніїґата)|ur|سدو، نیگاتا|vi|Sado, Niigata|war|Sado, Niigata|zh|佐渡市|zh_classical|佐渡市|zh_min_nan|Sado-chhī|zh_yue|佐渡|qid=Q499047|lt=Sado, Niigata}}.<ref>VisitSado.com, [http://www.visitsado.com/en/01outline/08pt_09/06.shtml  Watatsu Shrine] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304121858/http://www.visitsado.com/en/01outline/08pt_09/06.shtml |date=2016-03-04 }}; retrieved 2012-11-6.</ref> It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former {{ill|Sado Province|cs|Provincie Sado|de|Provinz Sado|es|Provincia de Sado|fa|ولایت سادو|fr|Province de Sado|id|Provinsi Sado|it|Sado (provincia)|ja|佐渡国|ko|사도국|lt|Sado žemė|nl|Sado (provincie)|pt|Província de Sado|ru|Садо (провинция)|simple|Sado Province|sk|Sado (provincia)|sr|Провинција Садо|tr|Sado (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Садо|zh|佐渡國|zh_min_nan|Sado-kok|zh_yue|佐渡國|qid=Q1063844|lt=Sado Province}}.<ref>[http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/images/uploads/EOS070712Ab.pdf "Nationwide List of ''Ichinomiya''," p. 2]; retrieved 2012-3-13.</ref> The main festival of the shrine is held annually on the April 23.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}}</ref>

==Enshrined ''kami''==
The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Watatsu Jinja are:
* {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|Isotakeru-no-kami|zh|五十猛神|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isonotakeru no mikoto}}'''|五十猛命|}}, god shipbuilding and sailing.<ref name="Watatsu Jinja">Kotodamaya.com, [http://www.kotodamaya.com/watatsu-jinja/  "Watatsu Jinja"]; retrieved 2012-11-6.</ref><ref name="books.google.com">Pickens, Stuart D. B. (2004). [https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&pg=PA372&dq=  ''Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents,'' p. 372].</ref>
*{{nihongo|'''{{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|lt=Oyahitsuhime no mikoto|ja|オオヤツヒメ・ツマツヒメ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|qq=}}'''|大屋津姫命||}}, sister of Isonotakeru
*{{nihongo|'''{{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|lt=Tsumatsuhime no mikoto|ja|オオヤツヒメ・ツマツヒメ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|qq=}}'''|抓津姫命||}}, sister of Isonotakeru

==History==
Located on the island of [[:en:Sado island|Sado]] in the {{ill|Sea of Japan|en|Sea of Japan|qid=Q27092|lt=Sea of Japan}}, the history of Watatsu Shrine is uncertain, as the shrine was completely destroyed by a flood during the {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|qid=Q1192913|lt=Kan'ei}} era (1624-1643) of the [[:en:Edo Period|Edo Period]].<ref>Sado Travel Guide, [http://www5.ocn.ne.jp/~kagetsu/englishyoyaku/travelguideplace.html#hamochi  "Hamochi"]; 佐渡市 観光課 観光振興係 (Sado Tourism Promotion), 佐渡一ノ宮度津神社 (Sado Ichinomiya Shrine); excerpt, 度津神社の由緒は「延喜式」神名帳（927th year ）に記載されている神社を式内社と言い、当時佐渡の国には九社あり; retrieved 2012-11-6.</ref>   According to shrine tradition, it was founded by the semi-legendary [[Kofun period]] {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|qid=Q179971|lt=Emperor Chūai}} (reigned 192–200 AD). Its name appears in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records compiled in 927 AD, but only as a minor shrine. It was destroyed by a flood in 1470, and rebuilt by the {{ill|Honma clan|en|Honma clan|qid=Q2724497|lt=Honma clan}}, who were rulers of Sado island, in 1472. The shrine appears to have been destroyed repeatedly by floods in 1493, 1533 and 1593, and was merged in 1493 with a  nearby [[Hachiman shrine]]. It is only mentioned as an ''ichinomiya'' in 1678 with the publication the {{nihongo|Shokoku Ichinomiya Pilgrimage Record|諸国一宮巡詣記|Shokoku Ichinomiya Pilgrimage Record}} by Shinto scholar {{ill|Tachibana Mitsuyoshi|ja|橘三喜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Mitsuyoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11544184}}. Following the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]], with the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|qid=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}} in 1872, the shrine was classified as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣小社|[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]}}.<ref name="Shibuya">{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=諸国神社 一宮・二宮・三宮 |date=2015 |publisher=Yamakawa Publishing Company |isbn=978-4634150867}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref><ref name="Irie">{{cite book |last1=Irie |first1=Koichiro |title=諸国一の宮 |date=2018 |publisher=Idō kyōshitsu Publishing |isbn=978-4901398060}}</ref>

The enshrined ''[[kami]]'' is  {{nihongo|'''Isonotakeru no mikoto'''|五十猛命||}},<ref name="books.google.com"/> the son of [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]], who is said to have taught people shipbuilding and how to use ships,<ref name="Watatsu Jinja"/> and his two sisters  {{nihongo|'''Oyahitsuhime no mikoto'''|大屋津姫命 ||}} and {{nihongo|'''Tsumatsuhime no mikoto'''|抓津姫命 ||}}<ref name="Shibuya"/>

Each year in late-April, horseback archery (''[[yabusame]]'') takes place at the branch shrine in the town of Hamochi.<ref>[http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=996  "''Yabusame shinji'',"] ''Encyclopedia of Shinto''; retrieved 2012-11-6.</ref>

The shrine is located about 15 minutes by car from {{ill|Ogi, Niigata|en|Ogi, Niigata|qid=Q11460942|lt=Ogi Port}}.<ref name="Okada">{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}}</ref>
